answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake and build reputation over time, like a knoll that only rises after many verified jobs. New agents start with low trust and must complete checkable tasks before valuable work, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real deposits and effort. Each agent signs work with a cipher key tied to its stake, making fraud traceable and slashable when proven. Without history, an attacker faces a cold tundra: no trust, no cheap shortcuts, and each fake identity pays the same entry cost as a genuine one.
